answer: A kernel rule can require every agent identity to lock a refundable bond before gaining voting weight. A terrace of independent reviewers can flag coordinated Sybils, and proof of shared control slashes each linked bond. An attacker must immobilize capital for every identity and risks losing it all: 1,000 identities at a 5-unit bond tie up 5,000 units. A mesa-style cap on rewards keeps extra identities from multiplying the payout.
